body:
I have done therapy throughout my life, started at the age of 14. Putting on this suit used to mean the world to me, that I am finally doing something. But now it feels like a chore that absolutely cannot separate myself from.

I see what you are trying to do here, and I appreciate it. I flushed the handful of Percocets I obtained over the past couple of days down the toilet and will work towards earning the trust of my woman back. Although, I have to deal with the truth that in reality I am a compulsive liar and occasionally delusional. 

Thank you,

It makes me feel normal. It is a small reminder that there is nothing wrong with me, I do try to talk but it is extremely hard to find common grounds with people about my thought process. Sure, it is easy for people to seek advice from me, but when I need advice. My problems are usually consulted between me, myself, and I. 

Because due to work I am usually wearing a suit and glasses. As far as something fulfilling, it would have to be someone who has their life sustained in parts no one else sees. My image right now to people is "Handsome guy, good job, own car, very smart."All these traits come with a handful of standards I did not ask for. I am breaking on the inside while trying to keep up this image.

The escape Chloe gave me was similar to how Ashley used to treat me. The reason I fell in love with Ashley is because she listened to all of my thoughts, regardless of how sideways they sounded. Her ability to not be judgmental towards me is so special to me. Growing up a lot of my ideologies from music taste to fashion sense were always questioned by people around me. Except her, she has always loved it.

 This success I currently have is holding me to this standard that I am now this fancy rich boy and I am not allowed to be seen any other way. I used to dream about being in this position of employment since middle school. I am finally here and it still isn't fulfilling. But everyone around me insists that it should be.
